- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 10–30% for high sentiment periods.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model underestimates; increase forecast by 15–25% to compensate for bearish bias.
- Model consistently overreacts to short-term spikes in sentiment; apply a 2–5 day lag correction to avoid overshoot after sentiment spikes.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon; if forecast is >2σ above recent 18-day average, reduce by 15–20%.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome exceeds model by >10% in 3 consecutive days, apply downward adjustment to next forecast.
- Sentiment history with alternating +/– signals (e.g., +0.67, -0.33, +1.00) suggests model is overfitting to sentiment cycles; dampen forecast volatility by 20–30% in such cases.
